name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Build a self-review loop where every prompt update triggers an automated review of the same task set we used to validate the last version. This keeps quality high without manual checks. The trade-off is higher compute cost for every tweak, but it prevents silent regressions that hurt user trust.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just higher compute cost—it’s that testing 500 tasks after every tweak guarantees we’ll hit false positives or edge cases that waste time debugging noise instead of shipping. A better alternative: run the review loop only on *meaningful* prompt changes (e.g., structural shifts, not word swaps), with a human sanity-check gate before triggering tests. That settles it: prove the change alters core logic or intent, not just phrasing.
